fields.label: App
fields.description: The app whose dock this layer arranges. Required: a dock belongs to an app, and a layer that named none would be one arrangement spanning every rail. An `Autocomplete` over installed apps rather than a Link, because there is no `App` doctype -- the house spelling, shared with `Sidebar.app` and `Desktop Icon.app`.

fields.label: User
fields.description: The person whose own arrangement this is. Blank means the app's own dock or the site's arrangement of it, told apart by `standard`.

fields.label: Standard
fields.description: Owned by the app: exported to `<app>/dock/<app>/<app>.json` and re-imported by migrate. This is the app layer, and the layer the other two are laid over. Ordinarily set via the Export to App action rather than by hand, which is why it is writable only in developer mode -- a standard dock with no exported file is an orphan and gets deleted on the next migrate.

fields.label: Mount On
fields.description: The app this one mounts on, for a companion app -- one with no rail of its own, whose entries live on a host's. Blank on every ordinary dock. An **app name** rather than a Link to a `Dock`: every consumer wants a string, and a pin aimed at a record would be a pin aimed at one of that app's three layers, which means nothing. App-layer only: `depends_on` hides it elsewhere and `validate` blanks it, because hiding a field does not stop an API write.

fields.label: Dock Items
fields.description: The ordered entries this layer has an opinion about. Row order is the arrangement; an entry this layer never names keeps its incoming order and follows the ones it does, which is how a newly installed app's modules still reach someone who has already arranged their dock.
